claim: The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so it is not emitted when the consuming project targets netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. Those are common MessagePack targets. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` already exists on both: .NET Framework 4.0+ and netstandard2.0, with AttributeTargets including Class. The derived criterion only allows conditional emission where the attribute does not exist. So the criterion 'All generated code is decorated' is not met for these targets, and generated code there still skews coverage. The README hunk documents this limitation as if it were inherent.

claim: Every emitted attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists in netstandard2.0 (netstandard.dll) and in .NET Framework 4.0+, and it is valid on classes there. So consumers compiling for netstandard2.0 or SDK-style net4x get generated formatters and resolvers with no attribute. 'All generated code is decorated' is not met for exactly the targets that do support the attribute. The guard is also inconsistent: legacy non-SDK net4x projects do not define NETFRAMEWORK and do get the attribute.

claim: The attribute is emitted only under `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`.
